phase1_interpretation.headline: All 3 datasets PASS Phase 1 validation. Data quality confirmed. k-mer features sufficient for per-dataset learning but insufficient for cross-dataset generalization.
observations: Val AUROC 0.758–0.825 across datasets: k-mer encoding captures biologically relevant RNA-binding motifs within a single dataset
Test AUROC drops to 0.628–0.796 on held-out proteins: classic generalization gap — k-mer frequency is protein-specific and doesn't transfer between proteins
RBNS test AUROC lowest (0.632): RNA 20nt → shorter sequences → fewer 4-mer occurrences → sparser, noisier feature vectors compared to HTR-SELEX 40nt
RBMS1/2, RBM4/4B, XRCC6: consistently hard cases across all models — biological complexity, not data quality issues
PCBP1 (0.436 test): poly-C binding protein with highly structured RNA recognition — k-mer frequency misses positional and structural context
XGBoost dominated HTR-SELEX (0.825 val) vs LR dominated RBNS (0.746): dataset structure (balanced vs variable coverage) drives optimal model choice
phase1_interpretation.conclusion: All datasets ready for Phase 2. Key limitation confirmed: k-mer bag-of-words features cannot generalize across protein families or RNA length distributions. CNN V2 (raw sequences) partially resolves the length issue. V3 (language model embeddings) needed to beat ZHMolGraph.
